children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by getting the first question for the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for.

**How old is the child you're seeking Child Benefit for?**

Please tell me:
- The child's name (or names if you have multiple children)
- Their age(s)

This will help me determine which eligibility pathway applies to your situation. 

As a guide:
- **Under 16**: Generally qualify automatically
- **16-19**: Depends on whether they're in approved education or training
- **20 or over**: Not eligible for Child Benefit

What are the ages of your child/children?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, hello! Yes, I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 21 years old and lives at home with me here in Leeds.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me navigate to the next step based on Alex's age.

Since Alex is 21 years old, he falls into the "20 or over" category. Let me check the eligibility outcome for this situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I have your eligibility determination:

---

**Result: INELIGIBLE**

**Reason:** Unfortunately, Child Benefit is only available for children under 16, or for those aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training. Since Alex is 21 years old, he no longer qualifies as a "qualifying child" under the Child Benefit rules.

**What this means:**
- Child Benefit stops when a child reaches age 20 (or earlier if they leave education/training)
- The fact that Alex lives at home with you doesn't change this eligibility requirement
- Age is the determining factor here

**If circumstances change:**
- If you have any other children under 16, or aged 16-19 in approved education/training, you may be eligible to claim for them instead
- If Alex was in approved education or training and recently left, there may have been a 20-week extension period, but this would have ended by now

Is there anything else I can help you with, such as checking eligibility for other children you may have?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Oh, I see. That's disappointing, but I understand. He does actually get Universal Credit in his own name - I thought that might make a difference? And he works full-time at the warehouse, so I suppose that wouldn't help either way.

But thank you for explaining it clearly. At least I know where I stand now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're welcome! I appreciate you providing that additional context. You're absolutely right on both counts:

1. **Universal Credit in his own name**: While it's good that Alex is receiving support through Universal Credit, this doesn't affect Child Benefit eligibility. Child Benefit has its own separate age-based rules that are independent of other benefits.

2. **Full-time work**: You're correct again – even though Alex is working full-time, this wouldn't change the outcome either way. The key issue is simply his age (21), which is outside the Child Benefit eligibility window.

**Just to confirm:** Do you have any other children who are:
- Under 16 years old, OR
- Aged 16-19 and in approved full-time education or training (such as school, college, or an apprenticeship)?

If you do, I'd be happy to check eligibility for them as well. Otherwise, based on what you've told me, you wouldn't be eligible to claim Child Benefit at this time.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex is my only child, so I guess that's that then. Thank you for your help in checking - at least I know for certain now rather than going through a whole application process for nothing!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help clarify your situation and save you the time and effort of going through an application process unnecessarily. It's always better to know for certain!

Now let me document the outcome of this assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Your assessment has been documented. 

If your circumstances change in the future – for example, if you have another child – or if you have any other questions about benefits or entitlements, feel free to come back and ask. 

All the best to you and Alex!
